chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who married a woman and stipulated for her: 'If he marries another woman to her, or abandons her, or takes a concubine for her, then she is divorced.' He ruled in that matter: 'The condition of God precedes your condition; if he wishes, he fulfills the condition for her, and if he wishes, he keeps her, takes another to her, and marries another to her.'

key_terms.شَرْطَ اللَّهِ: God's condition (referring to the husband's choice/discretion)
key_terms.شَرْطِكُمْ: Your condition (the stipulated condition in the marriage contract)
key_terms.وَفَى لَهَا بِالشَّرْطِ: He fulfilled the condition for her

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a wife's right of divorce if her husband marries another woman to her according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rules that the husband retains the primary right of choice (ikhtiyar) to either honor the stipulation and divorce his wife or keep her while marrying another, reflecting the principle that 'God's condition precedes yours.' This ruling highlights the flexibility in marital contracts within Shia jurisprudence, where the husband's discretion balances the wife's conditional right against the permissibility of polygyny. It underscores the legal maxim that specific contractual conditions are subordinate to the broader divine permission for a man to have up to four wives.
